instrument_repairs_made_during_this_task: evaluation/eval_parser.py::_match_key — identity was (indicator name, age_band, _variant_suffix), and _variant_suffix is derived FROM THE CODE. A standard whose code came out malformed therefore could not pair with its golden at all and reported as `dropped`, which removes it from field_stats and so from field_accuracy. Kentucky is the live case: the parser emitted bare TCPHS/IHFC/PARTO/PSGPB where the golden has HMW.1.1.TCPHS etc., and the suite reported coverage 0.846 with field accuracy 1.000 — a perfect score that existed only because the four malformed rows had been excluded from the denominator of the metric meant to catch them. Repair: the suffix is no longer part of the key; it is applied as a TIE-BREAKER inside grade_parser, used only when more than one candidate shares (name, age_band), which is the condition its own docstring already described. Tightening only. Verified score-neutral on AZ/CA/CO/TX (0 diffs across every field of every state report, re-grading identical cached output); CA's 39 proficiency-variant groups and TX's 10 still resolve through the tie-breaker. KY after repair: coverage 1.000, field accuracy 0.983, 8 real mismatches now visible. NV unchanged. Side benefit: measure_stability keys on _match_key too, so a run-to-run code change now counts as a field disagreement (_sig covers indicator.code and standard_id) instead of dropping the element from the comparison unseen — one of the two repairs Task 5 lists as a prerequisite.

evaluation/eval_parser.py::measure_stability — NOT REPAIRED, DIAGNOSED ONLY, and it blocks Task 5. It spawns its own N runs (stab-0..N) and compares them ONLY to each other; the run the suite actually GRADED is a separate call and is never in the comparison. On 2026-08-16 it reported field disagreement rate 0.000 and size stdev 0.00 for KY in the very same invocation whose graded output carried 4 malformed standard_ids — the graded run (18:19:22) fired and the five probe runs (18:22-18:33) did not. Before Task 5 spends its ~60 runs: (1) include the graded run in the comparison (N+1 observations, zero extra cost); (2) report the observed range, not only the rate ('1 of 6 runs differed in 8 cells' vs '5 runs, 0 disagreements'); (3) report the denominator and the time span. The _match_key repair above already fixed the other half of this instrument — identity no longer depends on the code, so a run-to-run code change counts as a disagreement instead of dropping the element from the comparison unseen.
defects_found: NV, detector, REPRODUCED KNOWN: the SS.CI.PK3 duplicate documented in CLAUDE.md. Two elements share the code; the defective twin's source_text is a truncated prefix and its title carries a fabricated tail ('with adult guidance', which appears 0 times in the extraction). Trigger visible in the extraction: NV p5 is a multi-column table whose reading order interleaves columns. The parser's 25 -> 24 collapse is the CORRECT compensation and must not be 'fixed'. This is NV's only hallucination — 1 of 53 detections.

NV, detector, PREDICTED BY CLAUDE.md: two of three domain codes wrong (Science 'S' -> 'Science', Technology 'T' -> 'TECH') while all 8 sub_strands correctly carry the document's XX.YY caption code. Mechanism pinned using detector.py's own guards: 'TECH' has derivable shape and is ungrounded so _resolve_code recomputed it, AND the golden code 'T' would ALSO be ungrounded in that source_text — so citing only the heading line defeats rule 4's code-recovery clause exactly as CLAUDE.md warns. 'Science' contains lowercase so nothing recomputed it; it lost to cross-chunk drift instead (log: canonical code 'Science', replaced ['SCIE']). NOTE Social Studies 'SS' is correct only BY COINCIDENCE — it is ungrounded, was recomputed, and derive_code_from_title('Social Studies') happens to return 'SS'. No NV standard_id is affected (NV indicator codes are the document's own); the cost is domain.code plus 4 propagated strand.code cells.
NV, detector: Science domain intro description truncated at 2410 of 3500 chars; propagates to 3 parser domain.description cells.

KY, parser, BLOCKING (not new): 4 indicator codes emitted UNQUALIFIED (bare TCPHS/IHFC/PARTO/PSGPB instead of HMW.1.1.TCPHS etc.), writing malformed Aurora primary keys of the form US-KY-2021-TCPHS. Domain/strand/sub_strand all correct; only the leaf lost its parent chain. NOT a detector-input problem — the HMW detector elements are structurally identical to the domains that parsed correctly. INTERMITTENT AND SAMPLING-DRIVEN, established from two independent records: 2 of 6 deployed batched runs fired, and 10 of 20 cached direct-path runs fired across 8 code hashes and 2 detection inputs, affecting 2 to 15 of 26 standards when they do. Causation is settled by two same-input clusters where code version, input and temperature are all identical: code hash c335e73a gave (graded 0, stab-0 6, stab-1 0, stab-2 4) and 6c193627 gave (graded 0, stab-0 4, stab-1 0, stab-2 15). DO NOT attribute this to a recent change — it appears at 8 distinct code hashes. DO NOT cite the direct-vs-batched disagreement on outputs/08-16-26 as evidence the paths differ; given the within-path variance it is a draw from the same distribution. Same defect CLASS as Task 1's CA 'Foundation N.N' finding but a DIFFERENT surface form, which matters: Task 1's recommended shape guard (block a code segment containing whitespace or a leading label word) would NOT catch this, because TCPHS has neither. The guard needs the parent-prefix condition added — exactly what the KY-BENCHMARK-CODE-NORMALIZED regression check asserts, and what caught it.
caveats: CORPUS TIER: every number in this folder is from the _only_subset tier (NV 15pp, KY 8pp), never full documents.

KY'S DETECTOR GOLDEN IS EXHAUSTIVE AND NV'S IS NOT, AND THE TWO MUST NOT BE PRESENTED THE SAME WAY. KY: 44 golden vs 44 in-scope detections with identical level counts and zero unmatched detections, so its raw precision 1.000 is a genuine hallucination-free result. NV: ceiling 0.7736 (41/53), and raw precision EQUALS the ceiling to four decimals, so the raw figure carries no information about correctness — NV's real number comes from the audit.

THE FP AUDIT VERDICTS HERE ARE AN UNSIGNED FIRST PASS. All 12 NV verdicts carry verified_by 'claude-first-pass-UNSIGNED'. Task 1b's methodology requires Emily as annotator of record, and the paper sentence 'all unmatched in-scope detections of the recorded run were manually audited by the author' is NOT true until she signs off. NV verified precision 0.981 is not quotable before then.

TASK 1b HAS NEVER BEEN RUN. paper/results/task1b_fp_audit.json does not exist, so Task 2 step 4's instruction to 'extend the Task 1b audit' had nothing to extend; the NV/KY audit was drafted standalone. Task 1b still owes the golden four their ~165 verdicts.
NV DESCRIPTION ACCURACY HAS A DENOMINATOR OF 3. Only 3 of NV's 41 golden elements annotate a description, so report 2/3 and never the rate 0.667. KY's denominator is 26 and is sound.

AGE-BAND DROPS CARRY NO INDEPENDENT SIGNAL WHEN RECALL IS 1.000: age_band_drops is a strict subset of missing_test_cases, so 'age-band drops: 0' follows arithmetically from recall 1.000 in both states and is not a separate confirmation.

CODE AND DESCRIPTION ACCURACY ARE CONDITIONED ON THE TITLE ALREADY MATCHING EXACTLY: both are graded over matched pairs only. Vacuous this run because recall is 1.000 in both states, but the metric names do not say so.

THE GRADED DEPTH MAP IS NOT THE ONE THAT DROVE THE GRADED DETECTION: evaluate_state calls infer_depth_map a second time purely for grading. Both states PASS and the two calls agreed, but a PASS is not proof the detection ran on a correct map.
PARSER FIELD ACCURACY AVERAGES OVER CELLS WHOSE GOLDEN IS NULL: 16.67% of graded cells in BOTH states. summary.json reports field_accuracy_over_asserted_cells_only alongside (NV 0.969, KY 0.980).

NEITHER BATCHING LAYER IS EXERCISED AT THIS CORPUS TIER: NV produces 5 chunks and KY 3 against MAX_CHUNKS_PER_BATCH=5, and both have 3 domains against MAX_DOMAINS_PER_BATCH=3, so detection and parsing each run as exactly one batch. No batching/scale claim may rest on these states; that is Task 6.

THE PARSER EVAL RUNS THE DIRECT PATH WHILE PRODUCTION RUNS THE BATCHED PATH, AND THEY DEMONSTRABLY DISAGREE HERE: on the identical KY detection at the identical code version, the batched production run emitted 0 unqualified indicator codes and this direct-path eval emitted 4. Consistent with Task 1's finding that parsing does not converge between paths.

THE KY STABILITY RESULT 0.000 IS NOT A DETERMINISM CLAIM. measure_stability excludes the graded run from its own comparison, and the graded run of that same invocation emitted 4 malformed standard_ids. Five probe runs agreeing is compatible with a defect that fires in a minority of runs; at N=5 that is not a null result.
